core.title: Give every feature definition a urn, a status, and a non-empty acceptance section
core.given: A file is a feature definition (a plan artifact), newly authored, edited, or already existing
core.when: the feature definition is written, reviewed, or validated
core.then: The feature definition declares a urn, a status, and a non-empty acceptance section.
prefer: Fill in the urn, the status, and at least one acceptance entry when first creating the feature definition.
Keep the acceptance section populated when restructuring a feature.
When an existing feature definition is found missing any of these fields, bring it into shape rather than treating pre-existing files as exempt.
avoid: Leaving the acceptance section as an empty collection or a placeholder just so the field is present.
Omitting the urn or the status on the assumption they are inferred from the file's path or from the product capability the feature lives in.
core.why: Downstream planning artifacts — component urns, component derivation, and product capability and plan coverage checks — presuppose a well-formed feature definition with these fields.
evidence: Parsing each feature definition (new, edited, or pre-existing) shows a urn field, a status field, and an acceptance section with at least one entry.

A finding is reported for any feature definition where the urn is missing, the status is missing, or the acceptance section is missing or empty — detected by parsing the file's current content, not only by diffing a change.
verification: Required fields: a urn, a status, and a non-empty acceptance section; the check tests presence of these fields (and non-emptiness of the acceptance section), not their values or shapes.

Detection of missing, removed, or empty fields is a verification step on the parsed content of the artifact, not an activation prerequisite; it runs on every feature definition in the check's scope, including files untouched by the current change.
Findings are derived from the artifact's current parsed content, not only from diffing a change.
Disposition is documentation-only (severity 2): findings are reported; this rule is not a strict-failing gate.
Which files count as feature definitions (their location and file kind) is not owned by this rule; recognition comes from the structure profile's role assignment.

fires: A new feature definition is created for a product capability.
An existing feature definition is edited (e.g. its acceptance section is restructured).
An existing feature definition is inspected or validated without any modification, and it lacks a status field or has an empty acceptance section.
A repository-wide validation pass checks all feature definitions, including ones untouched by the current change.
doesNotFire: A product capability or other plan artifact that is not a feature definition is created, edited, or inspected.
Code or test files are changed and no feature definition is involved.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete artifact kind that plays the feature-definition part of the plan-artifact role, so the core's 'feature definition' can be recognized in the stack.

How a file is recognized as a feature definition (assigned to the plan-artifact role by planner location and artifact kind), so activation works without this rule owning the exact recognition glob. In the reference stack the exact path glob is repository-specific and deferred, so no concrete placement pattern is asserted.
profileRequirements.bunValue: Feature files are identifiable by their planner location and YAML kind; the exact path glob is repository-specific (see context.repo-topology.idioms).

profileRequirements.meaning: How a feature definition declares its own urn — the field whose presence the check tests.

neutralityNotes: The artifact is called 'feature definition' in the core; its concrete kind (feature YAML) and recognition criterion (planner location plus file kind, exact path glob repository-specific) come from the profile via roles.plan_artifact.kinds and roles.assignment, and the urn field via urn.declaration. bun.json itself defers the exact path glob to repository topology, so the core asserts no concrete placement pattern (layout.plan_item would imply a concrete per-artifact path the reference does not state). The field names urn, status, and acceptance are treated as ATDD artifact vocabulary shared across stacks rather than stack-specific. The reference stack's concrete upstream artifact names (ioSeeds, DESIRED OUTCOMES) and the YAML-parse observer remain only in the Bun realization. Nothing else resisted neutralization; the rule has no exceptions, and no profile key was missing.
